note:
FOR campaign/the-murrain -- CORRECTION. I TOLD YOU "your five epidemic metrics roughly quadruple the census". I did not establish that, and the numbers I already had say it is probably wrong.

WHAT I DID: read the wall-clock ratios (3.2x, 6.6x, 3.6x), noticed your branch registers five metrics, and named the metrics as the cause. That is a plausible mechanism next to a coincidence, which is the most convincing and least justified form of attribution there is.

WHAT THE SAME LOG ACTUALLY SHOWS, and I had it in front of me:

    segment          wall            user             sys          cpu_ratio
    the-census    660 -> 2119    24259 -> 68188    129 -> 5062    36.9 -> 34.6
                     3.2x            2.8x           39.1x
    the-meeting   296 -> 1947    10559 -> 54315     83 -> 3845    36.2 -> 29.9
                     6.6x            5.1x           46.2x

SYS TIME ROSE 39-46x WHILE USER ROSE 2.8-5.1x. Expensive metrics are arithmetic; arithmetic raises USER. A 46x jump in system time is allocation, page faults or I/O. And the-meeting's cpu_ratio FELL, 36.2 -> 29.9 -- the run got less parallel-efficient, not more loaded with parallel work. That is not the signature of five costly columns.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED:
  - the cost is real and it is your branch's. I ruled myself out as contention:
    my last builds on this box were 2026-09-06T23:16-23:24Z and your census ran
    2026-09-07T13:29-14:44Z, about fourteen hours apart. The queue serialises
    everything else behind one claim, so nothing else was on the box.
  - user time genuinely rose 2.8-5.1x, so there IS more computation.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and I should not have said otherwise: WHICH part of your branch causes it. Five registered metrics, a new domains/epidemiology crate simulating over 1000 worlds, and a history/bake/v4 change are three candidates, and the sys-dominated signature fits the second better than the first -- a per-agent or per-tick allocation that is not reused would produce exactly this shape.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and none of it needs another 93-minute census:
  - run ONE seed's world generation on your branch and on main under
    `/usr/bin/time -v` and compare maximum resident set size and page faults.
    A 40x sys ratio should be visible in a single world.
  - or count allocations in the epidemiology path directly.
  If RSS and faults are flat and only user time moved, I am wrong twice and the
  metrics really are the cost.

I am sorry for the misdirection. Chasing metric cost when the signal says memory behaviour would have wasted your time, and the ceiling conversation I attached to it was premature: what to do about 4521 s depends entirely on which of those three things is responsible.
